Question: A disk of radius \(1\) rolls all the way around the inside of a square of side length \(s > 4\) and sweeps out a region of area \(A.\) A second disk of radius \(1\) rolls all the way around the outside of the same square and sweeps out a region of area \(2A.\) The value of \(s\) can be written as \(a+\dfrac{b\pi}{c},\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are positive integers and \(b\) and \(c\) are relatively prime. What is \(a+b+c?\)
Solution:
The disks sweep bands of width \(2\), their diameter. The corners behave differently inside and outside the square, so account for those pieces separately, as in [Figure 1](figures/2021_Fall_AMC_10A_Q19_official_solution_fig1.png).

For the inside motion, the untouched central square has side \(s-4\). Start with the surrounding band, of area \(s^2-(s-4)^2\). At each outer corner, a unit square in that band is only partly reached: the disk reaches a quarter-circle of radius \(1\) there. Removing four unit squares and adding four quarter-circles gives
\[
A=s^2-(s-4)^2-4+\pi=8s-20+\pi.
\]
Outside, the swept region consists of four rectangles, each of length \(s\) and width \(2\), and four quarter-circles of radius \(2\) around the vertices. Its area is \(8s+4\pi\).

The outside area is twice the inside area, so
\[
8s+4\pi=2(8s-20+\pi),\qquad s=5+\frac\pi4.
\]
Hence \(a+b+c=5+1+4=\boxed{10}\), choice A.
